doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Never needing a day job
summary: She has worked only in music for fifty years and has no experience of a day job.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: That’s okay because we’re going to return to that. I’m fascinated by your original, your songwriting. But you said when you went to New York you went there, you wanted to be a bona fide jazz singer. Did you have to pay dues in another way? In other words did you have to get a day job in order to pursue, to pay for your calling?

Hmm. I just realized, this is 2023. I’ve been doing this consecutively for fifty years plus now. Okay? And I’ve never done anything but music, anything but music. Even if I were in some acting thing I could sing. You know what I mean? I mean there was a part where you had to sing something, so I was never not singing for a living. That’s all I’ve ever done. I don’t know the first thing about waiting tables although I think I’m a pretty good chef myself and I’m happy to invite people over and serve them, but I don’t know anything and it’s kind of scary because it’s a good thing that I have some background with this and I’ve kind of developed a good — I think I’m a good teacher, I think I work well with young people, but I’ve never, I have no experience whatsoever out in a day job realm of life.
